messages:
jd_customer: Hey team — hitting a reproducible problem with SSE streams in prod. Streams often cut out at ~80–95s, payloads from the model are truncated JSON (partial output), then the client reconnects and sometimes receives duplicate chunks. ~10% of streaming sessions affected at peak. No obvious stacktrace on client, just closed socket. Also seeing intermittent 401 on reconnects for a subset of users. Repro steps at the end.

alex_support: Ugh. Thanks for reporting. A few quick Qs: is there a load balancer or reverse proxy (ALB/nginx) in front? Did this start after a deploy or config change? Do you have a request sample + headers and any connection logs?

jd_customer: Request sample: 
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-1'
```
Server log around disconnect (simplified):
```
[2026-03-12T18:02:13Z] conn=abcd1234 write error: broken pipe
[2026-03-12T18:02:13Z] conn=abcd1234 closed by client
```
Topography: AWS ALB -> sidecar nginx -> app (node/golang). ALB idle timeout is still default (60s). We added a client-side comment ping every 25s (`/:\n` via EventSource custom ping) after seeing earlier docs.

carla_sre: Two likely culprits: 1) LB or nginx is treating tiny comment pings as idle (or buffering them away) and closing TCP, 2) token TTL/refresh path returns 401 during reconnect and the client retries (flood) causing upstream resource stress. Also some proxies buffer small writes and won't flush until buffer is filled or connection closed, so a single `:\n` can be swallowed.

kevin_runtime: Adding to that: our streaming runtime expects backend to flush small SSE comments (or we explicitly send keepalive bytes). If the proxy buffers, the backend thinks connection is still open but client has been disconnected — results in partial output visible to the app and then a reset on the next write.

alex_support: Can you capture a tcpdump around a failing session and share a short pcap (or `tcpdump -A host <client_ip> and port 443 -w out.pcap`)? Also please paste the raw response headers you get from the client when it observes the socket close.

jd_customer: Will grab pcap. Quick additional note: when 401 occurs on reconnect, the client performs a refresh dance and then immediately reconnects on the same logical request which sometimes leads to duplicate events.

kevin_runtime: For an immediate mitigation you can try:
1) On nginx sidecar, ensure buffering is disabled and timeouts are increased:
```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_buffers 4 256k;
proxy_busy_buffers_size 256k;
proxy_read_timeout 300s;
proxy_send_timeout 300s;
keepalive_timeout 120s;
```
2) On ALB (or any L4/L7 LB) increase idle timeout to >120s (ALB default 60s).
3) In the app, write a slightly bigger keepalive payload at regular intervals (not just `:\n` but e.g. `: keepalive\n\n` or a 1–2 byte comment plus newline) and explicitly call flush on the response stream.

carla_sre: Also verify HTTP2/ALPN behavior — small data frames on HTTP/2 sometimes get coalesced. If using HTTP/2 TLS to LB, ensure the path doesn't reframe small pings.

alex_support: For the 401-on-reconnect issue: can you confirm token lifetime and refresh logic? If the reconnect flow attempts to connect with an expired/rotated token, we should return 401 and the client should pause/backoff before retrying. That prevents reconnect storms.

jd_customer: Token TTL is 60s in our test env (oops). We'll extend TTL and add proper refresh before reconnect. We saw about ~0.8% of reconnects hit 401.

kevin_runtime: Repro checklist for us (we'll try to reproduce in staging):
- Start a long-running SSE streaming session (server streaming tokens every 1s).
- Configure nginx with default buffering + ALB idle timeout 60s to emulate prod.
- Client sends comment pings `:\n` every 25s.
- Observe server write calls and check if comment pings reach backend.
- Capture server-side write errors and tcpdump at proxy + backend.
Commands to run:
```bash
# on client box (simulate reconnect):
python3 tools/sse_repro.py --url 'https://staging.redwood/stream' --ping-interval 25 --token-ttl 60
# on proxy host:
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <client_ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/sse_repro.pcap
```

carla_sre: Instrumentation checks to add:
- metric: `sse.disconnect_rate` (tagged by reason if possible)
- metric: `sse.partial_output_count`
- logs: `connection write failed` count by instance
- trace: time between last successful write and socket close for affected sessions

alex_support: Short-term mitigation plan for prod:
- Devs adjust ALB idle timeout to 180s (ops change)
- Enable `proxy_buffering off` on sidecars and add `proxy_read_timeout 180s`
- Update client to send slightly larger keepalive + backoff on 401 during reconnect
- Add idempotency via `Last-Event-ID` or server-side event-dedup (so duplicate chunks are no-ops)

kevin_runtime: I'll take ownership: I'll push a small server change to emit a 2-byte comment keepalive every 20s and call `flush()` explicitly. I'll also add event id headers so clients can dedupe. Testing/rollout plan: patch to staging in 2 hours, run repro script, then roll to canary.

ops_bot: INC-2341 created and assigned to kevin_runtime. Priority set P2.

billing_bot: Note: if the client reconnects repeatedly it may generate duplicate billable tokens. Recommend applying dedupe to billing pipeline for affected window (contact billing ops if you see unexpected spikes).

kevin_runtime: quick note for the triage: if tcpdump shows the client comment pings never leave ALB, it's a proxy/LB issue. If pings reach nginx but not the app, check nginx buffering. If pings reach the app but TCP is closed shortly after, check token TTL / auth handshake.

jd_customer: thanks — will gather pcap and token refresh logs and post back here. Appreciate the clear steps. :thumbsup:

ops_bot: follow-up: scheduled canary deploy window 2026-03-12T22:00Z -> 22:30Z for the keepalive patch.

kevin_runtime: I'll also add an alert: `sse.keepalive_missed > 3` per instance -> Pager to eng-sre.

jd_customer: ok posting pcap in a minute, and will extend token TTL as interim fix.

alex_support: Great — please ping when you upload pcap and the token logs. We'll keep monitoring and coordinate a canary once kevin confirms staging repro.
